title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance Annual General Adjustment 5% cap (Measure BB)
requirement: The Annual General Adjustment for fully covered units is capped at a maximum of 5%, even if the Rent Ordinance formula yields more; banked unused AGAs may still be applied. Landlords may petition for increases only for completed capital improvements.
coverage_conditions: Fully covered units include most multifamily properties built before 1980 and single-family homes with tenancies begun before 1996. Government-owned or -subsidized units are now fully or partially covered; post-1980 new construction, most single-family homes and condominiums are partially covered.

conditions.text: Government-owned or -subsidized units are now fully or partially covered depending on unit type and federal or state law.

coverage_quotes: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980
New Construction Units (units with a certificate of occupancy issued after 1980)
Government-owned or -subsidized rental units like Section 8 and Shelter + Care units are Now Fully or Partially Covered by the Rent Ordinance

exemptions: Units where the tenant shares kitchen or bath facilities with a landlord who did not live on the property at the start of the tenancy; units where federal law, state law or administrative regulation prohibits rent control (e.g. Section 202, Section 811, certain HUD-mortgaged projects) are only partially covered.
penalty: The Rent Board may adopt fines for noncompliance with the Ordinance's registration requirements, including failure to timely report tenancy information.
quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.
interaction: Units are fully or partially covered depending on whether federal law, state law or administrative regulation exempts the unit from the rent control provisions.

title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance just cause eviction requirements (Measure BB)
requirement: Tenants in covered units may be evicted only for just cause. Nonpayment eviction requires debt of at least one month's Fair Market Rent, eviction for refusing to sign a substantially similar lease is barred, and lease-breach eviction needs substantial actual harm.
coverage_conditions: Tenants in units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance.
quoted_span: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR as determined by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development for the fiscal year in which the rent is demanded.
